title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Nasdaq closed at a record high Tuesday, up ~0.5%, as chipmakers extended a 6-session rally (Philadelphia Semiconductor Index +2%); Dow fell 185 pts (-0.4%), S&P 500 roughly flat.

Markets: Brent crude fell for a 5th straight session, closing below $100/bbl (~$99.25) on hopes for Iran diplomacy at the UN, even as Trump floated an option to "annihilate" Iran; Iran reportedly proposed reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
Markets: Bitcoin held near $86,300. US equity futures point modestly higher this morning; flash September PMIs (manufacturing/services) due 9:45am ET.
Companies: Bank and brokerage stocks slid on fears AI agents (like Meta's new 'Muse') could automate financial decision-making; Charles Schwab fell more than 6%.
Companies: Chip/memory names rallied - Monolithic Power +8%, Sandisk +7%, Seagate and Micron each +5%.
Companies: Lennar jumped 6%+ after Berkshire Hathaway disclosed it boosted its stake to roughly 10%.
Macro/Policy: Fed Governor Michael Barr speaks today; markets still digesting last week's rate hike to 3.75%-4.00%, with some FOMC members open to another hike this year.
Macro/Policy: Earnings due today from General Mills, Cracker Barrel, Cintas and Paychex; UN General Assembly continues in NYC amid Iran tensions.
